   142	/-! ## §1. A zero sheaf of modules is finitely presented
   143	
   144	Mathlib carries no instance for this (`infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
   145	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`), so the `QuasicoherentData` is built by
   146	hand: one cover member `⊤`, no generators, no relations. -/
   147	
   148	namespace Scheme.Modules
   149	
   150	variable {Y : Scheme.{u}}
   151	
   152	/-- **The singleton family `{⊤}` covers the top of the opens site.**
   153	
   154	The one covering datum every "global" presentation needs, and the reason a *global*
   155	presentation of a sheaf of modules on `Y` is already a `QuasicoherentData`: the sieve
   156	`Sieve.ofObjects (fun _ => ⊤) V` is the top sieve at every open `V`, because
   157	`V ≤ ⊤` supplies the required arrow. -/
   158	theorem coversTop_singleton_top :
   159	    (Opens.grothendieckTopology (Y : TopCat)).CoversTop
   160	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) := by
   161	  intro V
   162	  have h : Sieve.ofObjects
   163	      (fun _ : PUnit.{u+1} => (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))) V = ⊤ := by
   164	    ext W _
   165	    simp only [Sieve.top_apply, iff_true]
   166	    exact ⟨PUnit.unit, ⟨homOfLE le_top⟩⟩
   167	  rw [h]
   168	  exact GrothendieckTopology.top_mem _ _
   169	
   170	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
   171	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
   172	/-- **The restriction functor to an open preserves zero morphisms.**
   173	
   174	`SheafOfModules.overFunctor` is `SheafOfModules.pushforward (𝟙 _)`, which acts as the
   175	identity on section groups, so the statement is `rfl` componentwise. It is proved
   176	rather than synthesized because instance search for
   177	`(overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms` exhausts its heartbeat budget
   178	(measured: `deterministic timeout at typeclass, 20000 heartbeats`) — the
   179	sheafification/slice-site instances it unfolds are the same blow-up
   180	`Scheme.Modules.presentationPullbackιOfQuasicoherentData` documents. -/
   181	theorem preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) :
   182	    (SheafOfModules.overFunctor Y.ringCatSheaf U).PreservesZeroMorphisms := by
   183	  constructor
   184	  intro _ _
   185	  apply SheafOfModules.hom_ext
   186	  apply PresheafOfModules.hom_ext
   187	  intro _
   188	  rfl
   189	
   190	/-- **The empty generating sections of a zero sheaf of modules.**
   191	
   192	No generators at all: the structure map `free PEmpty ⟶ M` is epi because *every*
   193	morphism into a zero object is, so there is nothing to generate. Stated for a general
   194	sheaf of rings on the opens site so that both `M` and its restrictions `M.over U`
   195	can use it. -/
   196	def zeroGeneratingSections
   197	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   198	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   199	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   200	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   201	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.GeneratingSections where
   202	  I := PEmpty.{u+1}
   203	  s j := PEmpty.elim j
   204	  epi := ⟨fun {_} g h _ => hM.eq_of_src g h⟩
   205	
   206	instance zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType
   207	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   208	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   209	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   210	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   211	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
   212	    (zeroGeneratingSections hM).IsFiniteType where
   213	  finite := (inferInstance : Finite PEmpty.{u+1})
   214	
   215	/-- **`free PEmpty` is an initial, hence zero, sheaf of modules.**
   216	
   217	There is exactly one morphism out of it into any target — `freeHomEquiv` turns a
   218	morphism `free PEmpty ⟶ Z` into a family of sections indexed by `PEmpty`, of which
   219	there is one — so it is initial, and an initial object in a category with zero
   220	morphisms is a zero object. -/
   221	theorem isZero_free_pempty
   222	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   223	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   224	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   225	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})] :
   226	    IsZero (SheafOfModules.free (R := R) PEmpty.{u+1}) :=
   227	  IsInitial.isZero <|
   228	    IsInitial.ofUnique (h := fun Z =>
   229	      ⟨⟨(SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).symm (fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩,
   230	        fun _ => (SheafOfModules.freeHomEquiv Z).injective (funext fun j => PEmpty.elim j)⟩)
   231	
   232	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules has an empty presentation** — no generators and no
   233	relations.
   234	
   235	The relations live in `kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π`, whose source
   236	`free PEmpty` is itself a zero object (`isZero_free_pempty`), so the kernel is zero
   237	too and the empty family generates it for the same reason. -/
   238	theorem isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections
   239	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   240	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   241	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   242	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   243	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) :
   244	    IsZero (kernel (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π) :=
   245	  haveI : Mono (zeroGeneratingSections hM).π := isZero_free_pempty.mono _
   246	  isZero_kernel_of_mono _
   247	
   248	noncomputable def zeroPresentation
   249	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   250	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   251	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   252	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   253	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : M.Presentation where
   254	  generators := zeroGeneratingSections hM
   255	  relations := zeroGeneratingSections (isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections hM)
   256	
   257	instance zeroPresentation_isFinite
   258	    {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
   259	    {R : Sheaf J RingCat.{u}} [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   260	    [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}]
   261	    [J.HasSheafCompose (forget₂ RingCat.{u} AddCommGrpCat.{u})]
   262	    {M : SheafOfModules.{u} R} (hM : IsZero M) : (zeroPresentation hM).IsFinite where
   263	  isFiniteType_generators := zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType hM
   264	  isFiniteType_relations :=
   265	    zeroGeneratingSections_isFiniteType (isZero_kernel_zeroGeneratingSections hM)
   266	
   267	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- slice-site sheafification blow-up
   268	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in
   269	/-- **The quasi-coherence datum of a zero sheaf of modules**: the singleton cover
   270	`{⊤}`, with the empty presentation on it.
   271	
   272	The restriction `M.over ⊤` of a zero module is zero
   273	(`preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor` plus `Functor.map_isZero`), so

   275	theorem isZero_over_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
   276	    (U : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat)) : IsZero (M.over U) :=
   277	  haveI := preservesZeroMorphisms_overFunctor (Y := Y) U

   283	    M.QuasicoherentData where
   284	  I := PUnit.{u+1}
   285	  X _ := (⊤ : TopologicalSpace.Opens (Y : TopCat))
   286	  coversTop := coversTop_singleton_top
   287	  presentation _ := zeroPresentation (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _)

   289	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 1600000 in -- as `zeroQuasicoherentData` above
   290	set_option maxHeartbeats 2000000 in

   292	    (zeroQuasicoherentData hM).IsFinitePresentation where
   293	  isFinite_presentation _ := zeroPresentation_isFinite (isZero_over_of_isZero hM _)

   297	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules on a scheme is finitely presented.**
   298	
   299	Absent from Mathlib: measured, `infer_instance` and `exact?` both fail on
   300	`(0 : Y.Modules).IsFinitePresentation`. This is the field of `Scheme.DivFamily` that
   301	had no route at `F = 0`, and it is why the empty divisor needed §1 rather than one

   303	theorem isFinitePresentation_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
   304	    M.IsFinitePresentation where
   305	  exists_quasicoherentData :=
   306	    ⟨(zeroQuasicoherentData hM).shrink,

   310	/-! ## §2. Flatness and proper support of a zero sheaf of modules -/
   311	
   312	/-- **The sections of a zero sheaf of modules over any open form a subsingleton.**
   313	
   314	`Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf` is additive, so it carries `M` to a zero presheaf of
   315	abelian groups, whose value at `V` is a zero object of `Ab` and hence a
   316	subsingleton. -/
   317	theorem subsingleton_sections_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M)
   318	    (V : Y.Opens) : Subsingleton Γ(M, V) :=
   319	  AddCommGrpCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
   320	    ((Functor.map_isZero (Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf Y) hM).obj _)
   321	
   322	/-- **A zero sheaf of modules is flat over any base morphism**, with no hypothesis on
   323	the morphism at all.
   324	
   325	`CoherentSheafFlat` asks each section module `Γ(M, V)` to be flat over `Γ(S, U)`. The
   326	section modules are subsingletons (`subsingleton_sections_of_isZero`), and a
   327	subsingleton module is flat. -/
   328	theorem coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero {S' : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ S') {M : Y.Modules}
   329	    (hM : IsZero M) : Scheme.CoherentSheafFlat g M := by
   330	  intro U _ V _ e
   331	  letI : Module Γ(S', U) Γ(M, V) := Module.compHom _ (g.appLE U V e).hom
   332	  haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM V
   333	  exact inferInstance
   334	
   335	/-- **The annihilator ideal sheaf of a zero sheaf of modules is `⊤`.**
   336	
   337	Each affine-local annihilator is the whole ring (`Module.annihilator_eq_top_iff` at a
   338	subsingleton module), and `ofIdeals` of the constant-`⊤` family is `⊤` because `⊤` is
   339	itself an ideal sheaf below it. -/
   340	theorem annihilator_of_isZero {M : Y.Modules} (hM : IsZero M) :
   341	    Scheme.Modules.annihilator M = ⊤ :=
   342	  top_le_iff.mp (le_sSup (by
   343	    intro U
   344	    haveI := subsingleton_sections_of_isZero hM U.1

     9	/-!
    10	# The divisor-support quasi-finiteness binder, reduced to its geometric core
    11	
    12	`AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`.
    13	
    14	## The obligation this file is about
    15	
    16	`Picard/DivPushforwardFlat.lean` carries, on every one of its theorems, the instance
    17	binder
    18	
    19	```
    20	[LocallyQuasiFinite (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom)]
    21	```
    22	
    23	— "the divisor `D ⊆ X_T` has finite fibres over `T`" — and says of it, in its own
    24	module docstring, that it "has no producer in this project", that
    25	`LocallyQuasiFinite` "occurs nowhere else in `Picard/`", and that it is
    26	"kernel-checked NOT derivable from `DivFamily`'s other fields". All three
    27	statements are true at HEAD and none of them is weakened here.
    28	
    29	What *was* never measured is **how much of that binder is geometry**. This file
    30	measures it, and the answer is that the binder is one topological statement away
    31	from free: two of the three inputs the mathlib criteria want are supplied by
    32	`DivFamily.properSupport`, which every family already carries.
    33	
    34	## What is proved here
    35	
    36	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyOfFiniteType_schematicSupportι_comp` and
    37	  `Scheme.Modules.quasiCompact_schematicSupportι_comp` — from
    38	  `HasProperSupport` alone, the support map is locally of finite type and
    39	  quasi-compact. Both by synthesis once `IsProper` is in scope; recorded as named
    40	  theorems because `HasProperSupport` is a `def`, not a class, so a consumer
    41	  writing `haveI := hps` gets **no** instance and the synthesis silently fails
    42	  (measured: `infer_instance` fails on both goals with the `def` in scope and
    43	  succeeds with the `IsProper` restatement).
    44	
    45	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_finite_fibers` —
    46	  the binder **is equivalent** to finiteness of each set-theoretic fibre of the
    47	  divisor over the base, for an arbitrary module with proper support over an
    48	  arbitrary morphism. No curve, no smoothness, no relative dimension, no
    49	  `DivFamily`.
    50	
    51	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_iff_isFinite_fiber` —
    52	  the same equivalence in the scheme-theoretic form, against
    53	  `IsFinite (…).fiberToSpecResidueField t`.
    54	
    55	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι_comp_of_finite_fibers` —
    56	  the direction a producer needs, as a standalone implication.
    57	
    58	* `Scheme.DivFamily.locallyQuasiFinite_of_finite_fibers` and
    59	  `Scheme.DivFamily.locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_fibers` — the same statements
    60	  at a `DivFamily`, where `properSupport` is a field, so the hypothesis list is
    61	  *only* the fibre finiteness.
    62	
    63	* `Scheme.Modules.locallyQuasiFinite_schematicSupportι` — for contrast, and
    64	  because it is the fact that makes the composite's failure informative: the
    65	  support immersion **on its own** is always locally quasi-finite, for every
    66	  module on every scheme, by `IsPreimmersion`. So nothing about the annihilator
    67	  or the support is what the binder is asking for; the whole content sits in the
    68	  projection to `T`.
    69	
    70	## What this does NOT do, stated because it is the natural over-reading
    71	
    72	* It does **not** produce the binder for any family. The remaining obligation is
    73	  the fibre finiteness, and that is where relative dimension one enters: on the
    74	  curve fibre `C_t` the divisor `D_t` is the zero scheme of a regular section of
    75	  an invertible ideal (`Picard/DivDegree.lean` has that fibre short exact
    76	  sequence in full — `Scheme.DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel` (the bare
    77	  name fails `#check`: it lives in the `Scheme.DivFamily` namespace, not
    78	  `Scheme.Modules`), `mono_fiber_kernel_ι`,
    79	  `fiberKernelIso`, `fiberCokernelIso`), hence `0`-dimensional, hence finite. That
    80	  step is genuinely absent and is not attempted here.
    81	
    82	* It does **not** close `AJC.picrep.divlocallyclosed`. D3′ proper is the
    83	  `ExistsUnique` statement about the Grassmannian locus; this file is upstream of
    84	  it.
    85	
    86	* It does **not** inhabit `Scheme.DivFamily`. `Picard/DivFamilyZero.lean`'s
    87	  `DivFamily.zero` is the tree's only producer, so every statement here is
    88	  testable at exactly one family.
    89	
    90	* It closes **no** `sorry`, and `Scheme.fgaPicardRepresentability` is untouched.
    91	  A shorter hypothesis list on the divisor side is not progress on the seam's
    92	  `rep`, and this file is verified with that theorem as a `sorryAx` control.
    93	
    94	## Why the reduction is worth landing separately
    95	
    96	The reduction is a repricing of D3′'s hypothesis: the binder is no longer an
    97	affine-local `RingHom.QuasiFinite` condition to be attacked at each site, but one
    98	fibre statement, with every scheme-level binder discharged from a field a family
    99	already carries.
   100	
   101	**"THREE ROWS" WAS AN OVERCOUNT AND IS WITHDRAWN — it is ONE row plus a partial
   102	contribution to a gate** (fresh-context audit, `I-1618`; the earlier text here, and
   103	this file's commit messages, said the reduction retires plumbing for D3′, D4′ and
   104	the local-constancy gate at once).
   105	
   106	* **D3′** — yes. This is that row's binder.
   107	* **D4′** — no. D4′ consumes D3′ and never binds `LocallyQuasiFinite` itself, so
   108	  counting it separately double-counts a single discharge.
   109	* **`Scheme.HasLocallyConstantDivDeg`** (`Picard/DivDegree.lean`) — partially. Its
   110	  own docstring names **two** inputs, "the finiteness/rank half of the campaign's
   111	  B3 rigid-pushforward engine **plus** relative-dimension-1 quasi-finiteness", and
   112	  its content is local constancy of a rank function. This file supplies at most the
   113	  second input.
   114	
   115	## References
   116	
   117	Blueprint: the campaign's D3′ node.

   119	Ex. `ex:DivC`. Mathlib: `AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/QuasiFinite.lean`
   120	(`locallyQuasiFinite_iff_finite_preimage_singleton`,
   121	`locallyQuasiFinite_iff_isFinite_fiber`,
   122	`LocallyQuasiFinite.of_finite_preimage_singleton`).
   123	-/

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivRepAffChallenge
     7	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0AtlasFromDivRepAff
     8	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.Pic0ChartAtlasCoupling
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam
    12	
    13	The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
    14	module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
    15	representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.
    16	
    17	The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
    18	two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
    19	representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.
    20	
    21	## Main declarations
    22	
    23	* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
    24	  genus-parameter divisor representer.
    25	* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
    27	  source opens.
    28	* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` represents `pic0TypeFunctor C`
    29	  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
    30	-/
    31	
    32	set_option autoImplicit false
    33	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    34	
    35	universe u
    36	
    37	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory Opposite
    38	
    39	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    40	
    41	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
    42	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    43	variable [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    44	
    45	noncomputable section
    46	
    47	/-- The universal widened divisor family carried by the chosen genus-parameter representer. -/
    48	def universalDivFamAffGenus :
    49	    divFamZarAff C (genus C) (divRepAffGenusScheme C) :=
    50	  (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv (𝟙 _)
    51	
    52	/-- Pulling back the chosen universal family gives the widened family classified by the
    53	corresponding morphism into the genus representer. -/
    54	theorem universalDivFamAffGenus_map {T : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    55	    (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
    56	    divFamZarAff.map C (genus C) q (universalDivFamAffGenus C)
    57	      = (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv q := by
    58	  have h := (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C).homEquiv_comp q
    59	    (𝟙 (divRepAffGenusScheme C))
    60	  rw [Category.comp_id] at h
    61	  exact h.symm
    62	
    63	/-- The widened Abel chart at the genus parameter, using the challenge curve's chosen divisor
    64	representer rather than accepting a representability witness as an argument. -/
    65	def abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    66	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    67	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    68	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ)) :
    69	    yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    70	  abelSigmaChartAff C (genus C) (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg
    71	
    72	/-- The structure morphism read from a genus-parameter widened Abel chart is the structure
    73	morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
    74	lemma chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus
    75	    (m : ℕ) (Z : (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    76	    (hdeg : Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k Z
    77	      = (m : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    78	    {ι : Type u} (i : ι) :
    79	    chartHom C (fun _ : ι => abelSigmaChartAffGenus C m Z hdeg) i
    80	      = (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom :=
    81	  chartHom_abelSigmaChartAff (divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy C) m Z hdeg i
    82	
    83	/-- A multi-index family of genus-parameter widened Abel charts, restricted to source opens.
    84	Different indices may use different twists and different opens, but they all use the same
    85	unconditional divisor representer. -/
    86	def affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    87	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    88	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
    89	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
    90	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
    91	    yoneda.obj (V i : Scheme) ⟶ (pic0SigmaSheaf C).1 :=
    92	  restrictChart (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)
    93	
    94	/-- The structure morphism of a restricted genus chart is the inclusion of its source open
    95	followed by the structure morphism of the chosen divisor representer. -/
    96	lemma chartHom_affineGenusChart {ι : Type u}
    97	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
    98	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
    99	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   100	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens) (i : ι) :
   101	    chartHom C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) i
   102	      = (V i).ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom := by
   103	  change chartHom C (fun _ : ι => restrictChart
   104	    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i)) i = _
   105	  exact (chartHom_restrictChart
   106	    (abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i)) (V i) i).trans
   107	      (congrArg ((V i).ι ≫ ·)
   108	        (chartHom_abelSigmaChartAffGenus C (m i) (Z i) (hdeg i) i))
   109	
   110	/-- The degree-zero Picard functor is represented by the glued object of any pointwise-covering
   111	family of open genus-parameter widened Abel charts.
   112	
   113	The divisor representation is construction data, not a hypothesis: it is supplied by
   114	`divFunctorAff_genus_representableBy`.  The two hypotheses are exactly the geometric inputs of
   115	Zariski local representability. -/
   116	def pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts {ι : Type u}
   117	    (m : ι → ℕ) (Z : ι → (C ⊗ overSpec k k).left.CurveDivisor)
   118	    (hdeg : ∀ i, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg k (Z i)
   119	      = (m i : ℤ) * classDeg k (thetaCechClass C) - (genus C : ℤ))
   120	    (V : ∀ _ : ι, (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens)
   121	    (hf : ∀ i, IsOpenImmersion.presheaf (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V i))
   122	    (hcov : PointwiseCoverage C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :
   123	    Σ J : Over (Spec (.of k)), (pic0TypeFunctor C).RepresentableBy J := by
   124	  letI : Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective Scheme.zariskiTopology
   125	      (Sigma.desc (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V)) :=
   126	    isLocallySurjective_sigmaDesc_of_pointwise C _ hcov
   127	  exact ⟨_, pic0RepresentableByOfCharts C (affineGenusChart C m Z hdeg V) hf⟩
   128	
   129	end
   130	
   131	end AlgebraicGeometry

    "body": "A DEGENERATE PARAMETER CAN BE THE ONE WHERE AN OBLIGATION IS PRINCIPLED, NOT THE ONE WHERE IT IS VACUOUS -- and the test that tells them apart is WHICH FIELD FAILS at the next value.\n\nThe workspace has a standing lesson in the other direction (degenerate-case-is-per-clause, substitute-trivial-value-in-layer-one): substituting a trivial value often shows a clause is CHEAP without exhibiting an inhabitant, and several AJCR rows were mispriced by exactly that conflation. So a lane that reaches for n = 0 should expect to be told it measured nothing.\n\nWHAT HAPPENED (pic-c, run 0092). The Pic^0 seam's rep antecedent had 93 consumers and 0 producers, every route gated on U2 at n = g. I built the degree-0 corner: the seven-field colength certificate closes with no hypothesis. That IS a vacuity-shaped move, and the check that decides whether it is one is not 'does the statement mention its object' -- it did -- but: ENUMERATE THE FIELDS AND ASK WHICH ONE BREAKS AT n = 1. Six of the seven are about zero modules being free and hold at every n; exactly one, rankAtStalk_glued = n, is what 0 makes vacuous. So the construction is not exploiting a degenerate object, it is exploiting a degenerate NUMBER in one clause, and the object it produces (a real certified family over every test ring) is inhabited and usable.\n\nTHE SECOND HALF IS THE SHARPER PART. The same substitution ALSO gave uniqueness -- effectivity of a local-equation system's divisor holds at every n and pins nothing; the certificate's degree identity holds at every n and pins nothing; their CONJUNCTION at 0 forces the divisor to be zero. Two facts each individually free, jointly decisive at one value. That is the shape worth looking for, and it is invisible if you price the two facts separately (gap-count-is-not-gap-cost).\n\nHOW TO APPLY. Before dismissing a degenerate parameter as measuring nothing, and before believing it: (a) enumerate the conjuncts of the obligation and name which single one the degenerate value kills; (b) check whether the value also makes a SECOND, independent fact decisive -- if it does, you have a theorem, not a vacuity; (c) state which binders the result still needs (mine needs Field twice for uniqueness and nothing for inhabitation) so the transfer question is visible rather than assumed. See [[nonvacuity-witness-must-satisfy-the-binders]] and [[witness-site-makes-consequent-free]] for the failure mode this is the complement of."

/-!
# The widened divisor representer at the Picard atlas seam

The widened divisor functor of a challenge curve is represented at the genus parameter.  This
module inserts that representation into the Abel construction and then into the Zariski-local
representability theorem for the degree-zero Picard functor.

The resulting chart family has no assumed divisor representation.  Its remaining inputs are the
two geometric conditions of the local-representability theorem: every restricted Abel map is a
representable open immersion, and the restricted maps cover the Picard sheaf pointwise.

## Main declarations

* `AlgebraicGeometry.abelSigmaChartAffGenus` is the widened Abel chart formed from the chosen
  genus-parameter divisor representer.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.universalDivFamAffGenus` is its universal widened divisor family.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.affineGenusChart` restricts a multi-index family of these maps to chosen
  source opens.
* `AlgebraicGeometry.pic0RepresentableByOfAffineGenusCharts` represents `pic0TypeFunctor C`
  once the restricted charts are open immersions and cover pointwise.
-/

# Concurrent-lane protocol (2026-07-16, from inbox I-0149's incidents — BINDING for parallel agent fleets)

Adopted after the 2026-07-16 evening wave's four incidents (I-0149). These rules extend the
standing handoff protocol (07-14/14b/15) for any session running two or more lanes in this
workspace.

## 1. Ledger commits: private index + compare-and-swap (the shared-index race)

All lanes commit through one `workspace.git`; concurrent `git add`+`commit` through the
SHARED index can interleave and record spurious deletions of another lane's
freshly-committed files (happened in `6197c9676`, 862 lines vanished from HEAD, restored
byte-identical in `a640fef5b`). Concurrent lanes MUST commit via a private index:

```bash
cd /home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree HEAD
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD -c user.name="Archon Horizon" -c user.email="archon-horizon@local" \
  commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "<math-first message>

Archon-Commit: agent
Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # CAS: fails if HEAD moved
unset GIT_INDEX_FILE
```

If the `update-ref` CAS fails (HEAD moved), re-read HEAD and repeat — never force.
ALWAYS verify afterward: `git --git-dir=$GD show --stat HEAD` must touch only your paths.
A single-lane session may keep the plain `add`+`commit` recipe, but must still verify.

### 1a. THE RECIPE ABOVE HAS A RACE — read HEAD ONCE, not twice (2026-07-28, run 0072)

**As written, the recipe reads `HEAD` twice**: once in `read-tree HEAD`, and again several lines
later in `PARENT=$(… rev-parse HEAD)`. If another lane's CAS lands **between those two reads**,
your tree is built from the *old* snapshot while your parent is the *new* commit — and
`update-ref` **succeeds**, because it only checks that the ref has not moved since `rev-parse`.
It never checks that the tree was built from that ref. You publish a stale tree, silently
reverting everything that landed in the window.

**Measured once, and the measurement is narrow — do not over-read it.** `e964967e8` has parent
`a1ef4d59c` and, diffed against *that parent*, deletes 95 lines of
`informal/w4-rep-critical-path.md`, 52 of `informal/w5-t4-worksheet.md` and 19 of
`Picard/Pic0ChartLocusIsOpen.lean` — exactly the restore `a1ef4d59c` had just performed, undone.
Its `read-tree` ran before `a1ef4d59c` landed; its parent was captured after. It staged explicit
paths and the pathspec *was* honoured: **the sweep came from the TREE BASE, not the pathspec**,
which is why "stage explicit files" is not a defence and why the symptom is indistinguishable
from §1b's shared-index staleness.

**Two other lanes audited their own CAS commits the same day (fifteen commits between them,
recipe verbatim) and found zero reverts.** That is consistent with this: the race only fires when
another lane's CAS lands inside your particular window, so clean commits are the expected
outcome, not evidence of absence. The discriminating question is not "did my commits look clean"
but "was my `read-tree` separated from my `rev-parse` by somebody else's commit". Treat §1a as
cheap insurance, not as a diagnosis of every mystery revert — and check §1b too.

**The fix is one line — capture the parent BEFORE the tree, and read-tree that sha:**

```bash
PARENT=$(git --git-dir=$GD rev-parse HEAD)     # ONCE, up front
export GIT_INDEX_FILE=$(mktemp)
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. read-tree $PARENT      # not "HEAD"
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. add <ONLY your paths…>
TREE=$(git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. write-tree)
COMMIT=$(git --git-dir=$GD … commit-tree $TREE -p $PARENT -m "…")
git --git-dir=$GD update-ref refs/heads/main $COMMIT $PARENT   # now genuinely atomic
```

Then a mid-recipe CAS by another lane makes `update-ref` **fail**, you re-read and retry, and the
protocol behaves as it was meant to. The verification step ("must touch only your paths") is what
catches it after the fact — run it every time, and read the file list, not just the count.

### 1b. The CAS recipe leaves the SHARED index permanently stale — this is by design, and it is armed

Added 2026-07-27 (run 0048 r5) after this failed a **third** time (`I-0366`: the shared index
was pinned to a pre-round-5 snapshot and a bare `git commit` would have deleted
`Picard/JacobianDataCharts.lean` and un-rooted it from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` in one commit).

The mechanism is not a bug in anyone's lane, it is the direct consequence of §1: a CAS commit
publishes a tree built in a **private** `GIT_INDEX_FILE` and moves the ref with `update-ref`.
The **shared** index is never touched, so the moment anybody commits, the shared index still
describes the previous HEAD — and `git status` then reports that difference as *staged changes*,
including **staged deletions** for any file the commit added. The longer a run goes, the further
the shared index drifts behind.

Consequences, all three binding:

1. **Never run a bare `git commit` (no `-a`, no pathspec) against `workspace.git`.** It publishes
   whatever the stale shared index holds, which is a reversion of other lanes' work.
2. **Before finishing, check and repair.** `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. status --porcelain | grep '^D'`
   must be empty. If it is not, repair with the **narrowest** form that covers your paths:
   `git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. reset -q -- <your project dir>/`. Prefer this to a whole-index
   `read-tree HEAD` when another run is live — a full reset can discard the other run's staging.
3. **Verify the worktree is the good copy before repairing.** `reset` makes the index match HEAD;
   that is only safe once you have confirmed the on-disk file is the one you want
   (`diff <(git --git-dir=$GD cat-file -p HEAD:<path>) <path>`).

Expect to repeat step 2 more than once in a long session: every CAS commit by any lane re-stales
the index, so a repair done early does not stay done.

## 2. The lake mutex is a mkdir DIRECTORY lock — never flock a file there

`/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock` is acquired by `mkdir` (atomic; a crash leaves a
directory that the next holder's timeout logic can reap). It is NOT a flock file: a lane
that runs `flock /tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock …` creates a plain FILE at the
path, and every mkdir-acquire loop then spins forever (this deadlocked all lanes
15:18–19:10 on 2026-07-16 until a human deleted it). Acquire pattern:

```bash
LOCK=/tmp/claude-1001/ajcr-locks/lake.lock
while ! mkdir "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null; do
  # (a) plain FILE at the path = a flock protocol-violation; reap immediately.
  if [ -f "$LOCK" ]; then echo "STALE: plain file at $LOCK (flock violation) — removing" >&2; rm -f "$LOCK"; continue; fi
  # (b) orphaned DIRECTORY from a crashed build (rmdir never ran). Reap on proof of death:
  if [ -d "$LOCK" ]; then
    holder=$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$holder" ] && ! kill -0 "$holder" 2>/dev/null; then
      echo "STALE: holder pid $holder dead — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
    # No pidfile (old-cohort holder): reap only if NO live lake build AND the dir is >15 min old.
    if [ -z "$holder" ] && ! pgrep -f 'lake build AlgebraicJacobian' >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && [ $(( $(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$LOCK" 2>/dev/null || date +%s) )) -gt 900 ]; then
      echo "STALE: no live build, lock >15min old — reaping" >&2; rm -rf "$LOCK"; continue
    fi
  fi
  sleep 10
done
echo $$ > "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null      # record holder so a later reaper can prove liveness via kill -0
# … lake build … ; rm -rf "$LOCK"      # release (rm -rf, not rmdir — the pidfile makes the dir non-empty)
```

### 2a. THE RELEASE IS AS DANGEROUS AS THE REAP — check the pidfile before `rm -rf` (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The acquire loop above is careful; the release (`rm -rf "$LOCK"`) is not, and that asymmetry
caused a real incident. **A lane removed the lock directory while its pidfile named a LIVE pid
belonging to another lane's build**, having printed `ALIVE` for that pid one line earlier.

The mechanism is worth stating because nothing in the recipe warns about it. The offending lane
had legitimately acquired the lock, and then **its own shell was killed by a harness timeout
while it held it**. On the next turn it reasoned "the lock is mine and my holder is dead, so
release it" — but in the interval a *different* lane had acquired the lock, so the pid in the
file had never been its own. The lane was running the release branch on a belief about history
rather than on a reading of the file.

> **Before `rm -rf "$LOCK"`, verify the pidfile still names YOUR pid.**
> `[ "$(cat "$LOCK/pid" 2>/dev/null)" = "$$" ] && rm -rf "$LOCK"`
> If it names anything else, the lock is not yours to release: say so and leave it alone.

Two corollaries:

* **"It was mine a minute ago" is not evidence**, especially when a harness can kill the shell
  between acquire and release. Every turn boundary is a window for another lane to take the lock.
* **Do not "repair" the mistake by re-creating the directory with the other lane's pid.**
  Fabricating a pidfile for a build you do not own makes the lock unreapable by its real owner
  and hides the incident. Report it on the thread and let the owner re-take it.

For long builds, prefer a form that cannot outlive its own hold: run the build detached with a
release trailing it in the *same* script, so the release is not a separate turn.

Two stale shapes, both now handled above (do NOT just `sleep` forever on either):
- A plain FILE at the lock path is by definition stale (mkdir makes directories) — reap immediately.
- An orphaned DIRECTORY from a build that crashed before `rm -rf` (the 2026-07-19 C4 incident,
  I-0257): the OLD acquire loop only checked for a file, so it spun forever on this. Writing
  `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` on acquire lets the next lane prove the holder is dead (`kill -0`) and reap
  safely; the no-pidfile branch (a holder from before this fix) falls back to "no live build + >15min".
  Never reap a directory whose pidfile names a LIVE pid — that is a real build in progress.

## 3. /tmp quota with >3 lanes

uid-1001 tmpfs quota exhaustion (EDQUOT) bricked every Bash call machine-wide
(~19:00–19:20). With more than ~3 concurrent lanes, keep scratch artifacts small, clean up
build temp dirs, and if Bash starts failing with quota errors, stop and report rather than
retry-looping.

## 4. The root import file: commit only your own lines (I-0153)

`AlgebraicJacobian.lean` is edited by every lane. Committing the WHOLE file via any recipe
sweeps siblings' uncommitted import lines into HEAD — the root then references files not yet
in HEAD (red for fresh checkouts), and a later sibling's whole-file commit can sweep or drop
YOUR line the same way. Before committing the root file: run
`git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD -- <project>/AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — if lines
other than yours differ, either (a) verify every swept import's file is already committed in
HEAD and say so in the commit message, or (b) construct the commit from HEAD's version plus
only your lines (apply a minimal patch to a temp checkout of the HEAD blob). Never commit a
root file that references uncommitted files without naming that in the message.

### 4a. A MINUS line in that diff is never yours (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The check above works. The failure mode is **misreading** it, and it happened again on
2026-07-28: the diff printed a `-import`/`+import` pair from a sibling lane's *uncommitted*
worktree edit, the committing lane read it as background noise, and the commit published the
sibling's replacement — dropping `Picard/DivRepAffPullIndep.lean` from the import closure.
The file stayed in HEAD and still compiled, but was reachable from nothing: **un-rooted**,
i.e. I-0153 again, from a lane that had run the I-0153 check.

So state the rule in a form that needs no judgement:

> **A `-import` line in that diff is never yours.** The only clean result is `+import <your
> file>` and nothing else. Any minus line means you are about to delete another lane's root
> entry — stop and explain it before committing. An unexplained `+import` you did not write
> is the same signal: a sibling's uncommitted edit is in your worktree copy, and a minus line
> usually accompanies it.

This is strictly stronger than "commit only your own lines", because you can intend that and
still sweep — staging the whole file is what publishes their edit, and the diff is your only
warning.

**Repair additively, never by reverting.** Restore the dropped import while **keeping** the
other lane's new one, then verify with a full root build (the 2026-07-28 repair: 9139 jobs,
exit 0, with the un-rooted file rebuilt). Reverting to your own earlier root blob discards
their work and turns one incident into two.

## 5. The AJCR mutex is for AJCR lake invocations only

No cross-workspace use (an OpenGA-Horizon agent squatted it ~25 min for its own
`lake cache get`, silently serializing AJCR lanes against unrelated work). Other
workspaces must use their own lock paths.

### 5a. Read it as per-PROJECT, not per-workspace (2026-07-28, run 0072)

The rule above says "cross-workspace", and that wording has a hole: **AJC and AJCR are two
projects in the SAME workspace.** Observed live on 2026-07-28 — the AJCR mutex was held for
over ten minutes while the only live `lake build` belonged to an `ajc-*` lane building
`MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge`, the sibling project. Same failure as the
OpenGA incident, not covered by the rule as written.

The lock path is `ajcr-locks`, so read the rule as: **only lanes building
`Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild` may take it.** AJC lanes need their own path
(`/tmp/claude-1001/ajc-locks/lake.lock`). Note the AJC task prompts do not mention a mutex
at all, which is very likely why an AJC lane reached for this one.

### 5b. Write the pidfile — the no-pidfile fallback cannot distinguish squatter from orphan

§2's acquire recipe writes `$$` into `$LOCK/pid` so a later lane can prove death via
`kill -0`. In the incident above the lock directory had **no pidfile**, so that branch could
not fire and the fallback ("no live `lake build AlgebraicJacobian` **and** dir >15 min old")
also could not fire — there *was* a live build, just not an AJCR one. Net effect: a
provably-non-AJCR holder is unreapable for 15 minutes.

Two consequences for a blocked lane, both applied in that incident:

* **Do not reap a directory whose holder you cannot prove dead**, even when you suspect a
  squatter. Reaping mid-build is worse than waiting.
* **Fall back to the narrowest check instead of blocking.** `lake env lean <file>` on the
  single changed file writes no shared build state and needs no lock; it is a faithful
  kernel check for that file. Record in the report that the mutex was unavailable and which
  check you substituted.

A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.

WHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.

NO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.

THE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.

THE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.

COROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].

VANISHING-VOCABULARY SPELLINGS ARE ONE ANTECEDENT -- and the commit that ships the 'reduced' producer often ships the iff that proves it is a re-spelling.

AJC DivFamilyZero.lean, AJC.picrep.divzero, pic-e runs 0095->0105. Over three rounds the same lane landed three producers of Div0-representable, each 'reducing' the obligation to a fresh vocabulary:
  _of_isZero               : IsZero x.F
  _of_forall_subsingleton_sections : forall V, Subsingleton Gamma(x.F,V)
  _of_forall_isEmpty_schematicSupport : IsEmpty(schematicSupport x.F)
Each docstring bills its antecedent as 'the sharpest/purest/most-geometric honest form.' At every DivFamily x.F is quasicoherent, and the file itself ships isZero_iff_forall_subsingleton_sections and isZero_iff_isEmpty_schematicSupport -- so the three antecedents are PROVABLY EQUIVALENT (all = IsZero x.F). None is weaker. The obligation HasFiberDeg 0 -> IsZero x.F is untouched; only the vocabulary on its RHS rotates.

THE TELL, sharper than I-1622: when a 'reduction' commit also lands an IFF between the new antecedent and the old one, the iff IS the proof that no reduction happened. Emptiness-of-support, subsingleton-sections, and IsZero are one node with three names; a producer parameterised on any of them is the same producer. Before crediting 'reduced to X', rw the shipped iffs and check whether the new antecedent closes the old goal with no hypotheses -- if it does, it is coordinates, not distance. The real distance for divzero lives in DivSupportQuasiFinite.lean (carrier bridge + degree-0=>empty-fibre), which no spelling of the RHS moves.

## I-1664
A LOCALISATION REDUCTION IS EMPTIED BY THE CONSUMER OWN OUTER QUANTIFIER, AND EVERY PER-STATEMENT CHECK PASSES.

MEASURED (pic-g, AJCR 0096 r7, Pic0RingZariskiLocal.lean; audit I-1657/I-1660, reproduced by me).

WHAT HAPPENED. I reduced an obligation P(A) at an arbitrary test algebra to a pointwise-local form: for every prime p of A, some f outside p with P(Localization.Away f). At a FIXED A that is a real reduction with no route back, and I verified it. I then composed it over all A into two producers of the goal object -- and those hypotheses are LOGICALLY EQUIVALENT to the global ones they were meant to weaken, because Localization.Away f is ITSELF a test algebra, so the consumer own forall-A already ranges over it. The converse is one line with the trivial witness f = 1.

## I-1642
A THREE-LANE COMPOSITION IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY PER-ROW CHECK, AND THE ROWS WILL EACH TELL YOU THE WORK IS ELSEWHERE.

WHAT HAPPENED (pic-e, AJC, 0095 r6). Three sorry-free theorems from three different lanes composed into a verbatim derivation of the project's central sorry from the classical pointed theorem: the unconditional finite-GALOIS-level rational point (Curve/), the picSharp->picEt transport (PicEtSubcanonical), and the lftFree descent step with hq and hcov already internal (PicEtGaloisQuotient). Eleven declarations, all axiom-clean, three commits.

NO ROW MENTIONED THE OTHER TWO. The descent-assembly row listed FOUR open inputs; three were already discharged elsewhere. The seam docstring's own 'what remains' sentence listed three items, one of which was closed and one of which was DONE-AND-CALLED-REMAINING. Every row was individually plausible and internally consistent; the composition existed only across them.

THE MECHANISM, and why the usual checks miss it: each row is maintained by the lane that owns it, and a lane records what IT owes, not what another lane has since supplied. So a row goes stale in the CHEAP direction -- it schedules work that exists -- and nothing re-reads it, because a list of remaining obligations reads as self-criticism. Same asymmetry as [[gap-list-is-the-least-audited-prose]] and [[unavoidable-is-not-geometric]], but distributed: no single sentence is wrong enough to notice.

THE CHECK THAT FINDS IT, and it is cheap: take the consumer theorem's LITERAL binder list -- #check the one a costing tells you to aim at -- and ask of EACH binder, separately, 'does a producer for exactly this exist at HEAD?'. Not 'is this gap open' (the row answers that) but 'is this BINDER discharged'. At the spelling that matters, seamClauseOne_of_hasGaloisQuotient_lftFree, three of four were gone and the fourth was an instance binder no row named. A four-item gap list and a one-item binder list were both accurate about different things.

COROLLARY, the part that cost me a withdrawal: after composing, price the RESULT against the WEAKEST antecedent your proof consumes, not the shape the hand-off wants. My first antecedent carried IsSeparated, which is provably free from the conclusion's own representation, and a reduction whose antecedent contains a free conjunct misreports exactly the number it exists to report. Related: [[price-the-consumer-carrier]], [[audit-the-goals-antecedents-not-the-lemmas]].
